units.title: Expressions and Real Numbers
units.blurb: Know the number system and read the structure of an expression.

units.title: Solving Equations
units.blurb: Solve equations with fractions, literal equations and absolute values, and explain every step.

units.title: Inequalities
units.blurb: Solve and graph inequalities, including compound and absolute value inequalities.

units.title: Functions
units.blurb: Use function notation, read graphs, and describe how outputs change.

units.title: Linear Functions
units.blurb: Write and use every form of a line, and model with linear functions.

units.title: Systems of Equations
units.blurb: Solve systems by elimination, model with them, and solve systems of inequalities.

units.title: Exponents and Radicals
units.blurb: Extend exponents to fractions and work with square roots.

units.title: Exponential Functions
units.blurb: Model growth and decay that multiplies by the same factor each step.

units.title: Factoring
units.blurb: Undo multiplication to write polynomials as products.

units.title: Quadratic Functions and Equations
units.blurb: Graph parabolas and solve quadratic equations four ways.

units.title: Data and Statistics
units.blurb: Summarize two-variable data and judge what it does and does not show.

topics.title: The Real Number System
topics.short: Sort numbers into natural, whole, integer, rational and irrational.
topics.trouble: Students think every square root is irrational, or that an integer like −4 is not a rational number.

topics.title: Rational and Irrational Sums and Products
topics.short: Decide whether a sum or product is rational or irrational, and say why.
topics.trouble: Students assume the sum of two irrational numbers must be irrational, missing cases like √2 + (−√2) = 0.

topics.title: Evaluating Expressions with Negatives and Powers
topics.short: Substitute values, including negatives, and follow the order of operations.
topics.trouble: Students substitute x = −3 into x² without parentheses and get −9, or treat −3² as (−3)².

topics.title: Terms, Factors and Coefficients
topics.short: Name the parts of an expression and what each one means.
topics.trouble: Students miss that the term in 5 − 3x is −3x, or that the coefficient of x alone is 1.

topics.title: Units and Conversion Factors
topics.short: Multiply by unit fractions to convert rates and keep track of units.
topics.trouble: Students multiply by a conversion factor upside down because they do not check which units cancel.

topics.title: Why Each Step Keeps the Balance
topics.short: Every step does the same thing to both sides, so the solutions stay the same.
topics.trouble: Students "move a term across and flip its sign" as a magic rule, then apply it to a term inside a product.

topics.title: Clearing Fractions and Decimals
topics.short: Multiply every term by the common denominator to get whole numbers.
topics.trouble: Students multiply only the fraction terms by the common denominator and leave the whole-number terms unchanged.

topics.title: Writing Equations from Words
topics.short: Translate a situation into an equation, then solve it.
topics.trouble: Students translate "5 less than x" as 5 − x instead of x − 5.

topics.title: Distance, Rate and Time Problems
topics.short: Use d = rt with a table to set up motion problems.
topics.trouble: Students add the two speeds when the objects move in the same direction, or mix minutes with hours.

topics.title: Solving for a Variable
topics.short: Rearrange a formula to isolate the letter you want.
topics.trouble: Students divide only one term by the coefficient, writing (y − b)/m as y − b/m.

topics.title: Absolute Value Equations
topics.short: Isolate the absolute value, then solve for both distances.
topics.trouble: Students keep only the positive case, or split into two cases before isolating the absolute value.

topics.title: Multi-Step Inequalities
topics.short: Solve like an equation, flipping the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative.
topics.trouble: Students forget to reverse the inequality after dividing by a negative, or reverse it after subtracting a negative.

topics.title: Inequality Word Problems
topics.short: Write and solve inequalities for "at least," "at most" and "no more than."
topics.trouble: Students use > for "at least" and forget that answers must make sense, such as whole numbers of tickets.

topics.title: Compound Inequalities
topics.short: Solve "and" and "or" inequalities and graph them.
topics.trouble: Students write an "or" solution like x < −2 or x > 5 as 5 < x < −2.

topics.title: Absolute Value Inequalities
topics.short: Turn |x − a| < b into an "and" and |x − a| > b into an "or."
topics.trouble: Students write |x| > 3 as −3 > x > 3, a statement no number can satisfy.

topics.title: Function Notation
topics.short: f(3) is the output when the input is 3.
topics.trouble: Students read f(x) as "f times x" and compute f(3) as 3f.

topics.title: Finding Inputs from Outputs
topics.short: Solve f(x) = k to find which inputs give an output.
topics.trouble: Students confuse f(2), an output, with the solution of f(x) = 2, an input.

topics.title: Domain and Range
topics.short: Find the allowed inputs and the possible outputs.
topics.trouble: Students read the range along the x-axis, or forget that the domain of a real situation is limited.

topics.title: Intercepts, Increasing and Decreasing
topics.short: Read where a graph crosses the axes, rises, falls and peaks.
topics.trouble: Students describe "increasing" by looking right to left, or give a point when an interval is asked for.

topics.title: Average Rate of Change
topics.short: Divide the change in output by the change in input over an interval.
topics.trouble: Students divide the change in x by the change in y, or use the x-values in place of the outputs.

topics.title: Sequences as Functions
topics.short: A sequence is a function whose inputs are 1, 2, 3, ….

topics.title: Arithmetic Sequences
topics.short: Add the same amount each time; aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d.
topics.trouble: Students write aₙ = a₁ + nd, which is off by one step.

topics.title: Piecewise Functions
topics.short: Use the rule that matches the input's interval.
topics.trouble: Students evaluate with the wrong piece at a boundary because they ignore whether the endpoint is included.

topics.title: Graphs of Absolute Value Functions
topics.short: Graph V-shapes and see them as two linear pieces.

topics.title: Step Functions
topics.short: Graph functions like the floor function that jump between flat steps.
topics.trouble: Students connect the steps with vertical lines, which breaks the function rule.

topics.title: Shifting and Stretching Graphs
topics.short: See how f(x) + k, f(x − h), af(x) and f(−x) move a graph.
topics.trouble: Students shift f(x − 3) to the left because of the minus sign, when it moves right.

topics.title: A Graph Shows Every Solution
topics.short: Every point on the graph of an equation makes it true, and no other point does.
topics.trouble: Students check a point by looking at the picture instead of substituting it into the equation.

topics.title: Point-Slope Form
topics.short: Write a line from a point and a slope: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).
topics.trouble: Students read the point from y − 2 = 3(x + 1) as (1, 2) instead of (−1, 2).

topics.title: Line Through Two Points
topics.short: Find the slope, then use a point to write the equation.
topics.trouble: Students subtract the coordinates in different orders on top and bottom, which flips the sign of the slope.

topics.title: Standard Form and Intercepts
topics.short: Graph Ax + By = C quickly using its two intercepts.
topics.trouble: Students find an intercept by setting the same variable to 0 that they are solving for.

topics.title: Horizontal and Vertical Lines
topics.short: y = k is flat with slope 0; x = h is vertical with no slope.
topics.trouble: Students graph x = 3 as a horizontal line, and say a vertical line has slope 0.

topics.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
topics.short: Parallel lines share a slope; perpendicular slopes multiply to −1.
topics.trouble: Students make a perpendicular slope negative but forget to take the reciprocal, or the reverse.

topics.title: Linear Models in Context
topics.short: Interpret the slope as a rate and the intercept as a starting value.
topics.trouble: Students read the y-intercept as a rate, or give the slope without its units.

topics.title: Inverse of a Linear Function
topics.short: Undo a linear function by swapping inputs and outputs.
topics.trouble: Students take the inverse of f(x) = 2x + 3 as 1/(2x + 3), confusing an inverse with a reciprocal.

topics.title: Linear Inequalities in Two Variables
topics.short: Graph the boundary line and shade the side that works.
topics.trouble: Students shade the wrong side when the inequality is not solved for y, or use a solid line for a strict inequality.

topics.title: Elimination
topics.short: Add the equations so one variable cancels.
topics.trouble: Students subtract one equation from the other but change the sign of only the first term.

topics.title: Elimination with Multiplying First
topics.short: Scale one or both equations so a variable will cancel.
topics.trouble: Students multiply only the left side of an equation, forgetting the constant on the right.

topics.title: Systems Word Problems
topics.short: Name two unknowns, write two equations, and solve.
topics.trouble: Students write two equations that say the same thing, or never say what each variable stands for.

topics.title: Systems of Linear Inequalities
topics.short: Find the region where both shadings overlap.
topics.trouble: Students shade each inequality but report the union of the regions instead of the overlap.

topics.title: Fractional Exponents
topics.short: x^(1/n) means the nth root of x, and x^(m/n) its mth power.
topics.trouble: Students compute 8^(1/3) as 8/3, or 16^(3/4) as 12.

topics.title: Rules with Fractional Exponents
topics.short: Use the exponent rules to simplify roots written as powers.
topics.trouble: Students add the exponents when raising a power to a power.

topics.title: Simplifying Square Roots
topics.short: Pull perfect-square factors out: √72 = 6√2.
topics.trouble: Students split a root over a sum, writing √(9 + 16) = 3 + 4.

topics.title: Adding and Multiplying Radicals
topics.short: Combine like radicals and multiply roots.
topics.trouble: Students add the radicands, writing √2 + √3 = √5.

topics.title: Exponential Functions
topics.short: In f(x) = a·bˣ, the output multiplies by b each time x goes up by 1.
topics.trouble: Students mix up 2ˣ with x², or multiply the base and the coefficient first so 3·2ˣ becomes 6ˣ.

topics.title: Linear vs Exponential Change
topics.short: Linear grows by equal differences; exponential grows by equal factors.
topics.trouble: Students judge by the first few values and miss that exponential growth eventually passes any linear growth.

topics.title: Geometric Sequences
topics.short: Multiply by the same ratio each time; aₙ = a₁·rⁿ⁻¹.
topics.trouble: Students use n instead of n − 1 in the exponent, or add the ratio instead of multiplying.

topics.title: Growth and Decay Rates
topics.short: A 5% increase multiplies by 1.05; a 5% decrease by 0.95.
topics.trouble: Students use 0.05 as the growth factor instead of 1.05, or 1.05 for a decrease.

topics.title: Writing Exponential Models
topics.short: Build a = a₀·bᵗ from a starting value and a rate or two data points.
topics.trouble: Students fit a linear model to data that changes by a constant ratio.

topics.title: Rewriting Exponential Expressions
topics.short: Use exponent rules to change a yearly rate into a monthly one, and back.
topics.trouble: Students divide a yearly growth rate by 12 to get a monthly rate, ignoring compounding.

topics.title: Polynomials: Degree and Standard Form
topics.short: Name terms, degree and leading coefficient, and order terms by degree.
topics.trouble: Students give the degree as the number of terms, or the exponent of the first term written.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Polynomials
topics.short: Combine like terms; subtracting changes the sign of every term.
topics.trouble: Students change the sign of only the first term of the polynomial being subtracted.

topics.title: Multiplying by a Monomial
topics.short: Distribute and use exponent rules on each term.
topics.trouble: Students multiply the monomial by the first term only.

topics.title: Multiplying Binomials
topics.short: Multiply each term by each term; an area model keeps track.
topics.trouble: Students write (x + 3)² as x² + 9, dropping the two middle rectangles.

topics.title: Special Products
topics.short: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².
topics.trouble: Students square each term separately and miss the 2ab term.

topics.title: Multiplying Longer Polynomials
topics.short: Multiply polynomials with any number of terms.
topics.trouble: Students lose a term in the bookkeeping, or forget to combine like terms at the end.

topics.title: Factoring Out the GCF
topics.short: Write 6x² + 9x as 3x(2x + 3).
topics.trouble: Students leave nothing behind when a whole term is factored out, writing 3x + 3 = 3(x) instead of 3(x + 1).

topics.title: Factoring x² + bx + c
topics.short: Find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b.
topics.trouble: Students find a pair that multiplies to c but ignore the signs, so the middle term comes out wrong.

topics.title: Factoring ax² + bx + c
topics.short: Split the middle term using ac, then group.
topics.trouble: Students factor as if a were 1, and never check by multiplying back out.

topics.title: Factoring Special Products
topics.short: Spot differences of squares and perfect-square trinomials.
topics.trouble: Students factor x² + 9 as (x + 3)(x − 3), not seeing that a sum of squares does not factor over the reals.

topics.title: Factoring by Grouping
topics.short: Group terms in pairs and pull out a shared binomial.
topics.trouble: Students factor −3 out of the second pair as +3 and end with mismatched binomials.

topics.title: Factoring Completely
topics.short: Take out the GCF first, then keep factoring until nothing more factors.
topics.trouble: Students stop after one step, leaving x² − 4 inside a product.

topics.title: Graphs of Quadratic Functions
topics.short: A parabola has a vertex, an axis of symmetry and opens up or down.
topics.trouble: Students think a larger coefficient a makes the parabola wider, when it makes it narrower.

topics.title: Vertex Form
topics.short: In y = a(x − h)² + k the vertex is (h, k).
topics.trouble: Students read the vertex of y = (x − 2)² + 3 as (−2, 3).

topics.title: Solving by Factoring
topics.short: If a product is 0, one of the factors must be 0.
topics.trouble: Students set each factor equal to 6 when (x − 2)(x − 3) = 6, though the rule only works for 0.

topics.title: Zeros and Factored Form
topics.short: The zeros of a(x − p)(x − q) are p and q, where the graph meets the x-axis.
topics.trouble: Students read the zeros of (x + 4)(x − 1) as 4 and −1.

topics.title: Solving by Square Roots
topics.short: Isolate the square, then take both the positive and negative roots.
topics.trouble: Students keep only the positive root of x² = 25, or take the root before isolating the square.

topics.title: Completing the Square
topics.short: Add (b/2)² to make a perfect square, then solve or find the vertex.
topics.trouble: Students add (b/2)² to one side only, or forget to divide by a first.

topics.title: The Quadratic Formula
topics.short: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a solves any quadratic.
topics.trouble: Students divide only the square root by 2a, or compute −b² when b is negative.

topics.title: The Discriminant
topics.short: b² − 4ac tells how many real solutions there are.
topics.trouble: Students think a negative discriminant means they made an arithmetic slip, when it means the parabola never meets the x-axis.

topics.title: Quadratic Models
topics.short: Use parabolas for falling objects and areas, and read the vertex and zeros in context.
topics.trouble: Students report both roots in a time problem, including a negative time that makes no sense.

topics.title: Line and Parabola Systems
topics.short: Find where a line meets a parabola by substitution.
topics.trouble: Students stop at the x-values and never find the matching y-values.

topics.title: Solving f(x) = g(x) with Graphs
topics.short: The x-coordinates where two graphs meet solve f(x) = g(x).
topics.trouble: Students give the y-coordinate of the intersection as the solution of f(x) = g(x).

topics.title: Comparing Linear, Quadratic and Exponential Models
topics.short: Choose a model by looking at differences and ratios in data.
topics.trouble: Students fit any curved data with a quadratic, without checking for constant ratios.

topics.title: Two-Way Tables and Relative Frequency
topics.short: Use row and column percents to look for associations.
topics.trouble: Students divide by the grand total when a question asks for a conditional percent within one row.

topics.title: Lines of Fit and Residuals
topics.short: Fit a line to data and use residuals to judge the fit.
topics.trouble: Students compute residuals as predicted minus actual, flipping their signs.

topics.title: Correlation and Causation
topics.short: The correlation coefficient measures linear strength; it does not prove cause.
topics.trouble: Students conclude that one variable causes the other just because they are strongly correlated.
